title: Intel TCMI Hardware Telemetry (Metrics Manager)
description: Unified T/C/M/I + R hardware telemetry for robotics / Edge AI / physical AI on Intel platforms, served by the Metrics Manager microservice.

panels.title: CPU Package + DRAM Power (RAPL = Running Average Power Limit)
panels.description: CPU package + DRAM RAPL power via intel_powerstat.

panels.title: Platform (psys) Power — NEW
panels.description: Total board power (CPU+iGPU+NPU+mem) from RAPL platform domain. Filled by the rapl_reader.py execd reader — intel_powerstat cannot see psys.

panels.title: CPU Temperature (package + per-core)
panels.description: coretemp package + per-core, via inputs.temp.

panels.title: NVMe + Board Temperature
panels.description: NVMe Composite + ACPI board thermal zone.

panels.title: NPU (Neural Processing Unit) Power / Temperature
panels.description: Intel NPU via PMT = Platform Monitoring Technology (npu_reader.py). power_state: PCI runtime-PM state, 0=D0 active .. 4=D3cold (−1=unknown).

panels.title: Uncore Frequency
panels.description: Current uncore (ring/LLC) frequency.

panels.title: CPU Busy %
panels.description: 100 − idle. Aggregate CPU utilisation.

panels.title: GPU Busy %
panels.description: Max across GPU engines (rcs/ccs/vcs/bcs/vecs) via qmassa.

panels.title: NPU Busy %
panels.description: Intel NPU utilisation via PMT.

panels.title: RAM Used %
panels.description: System memory utilisation.

panels.title: CPU / GPU / NPU Busy % — Time Series
panels.description: Compute utilisation across all three accelerators.

panels.title: Per-core CPU Frequency
panels.description: Per-core frequency via intel_powerstat.

panels.title: GPU Frequency (requested vs actual)
panels.description: Driver-requested (cur_freq) vs achieved (act_freq) GPU frequency per GT, via gpu_throttle_reader.py. A gap = the GPU couldn't hold the requested clock.

panels.title: GPU Engine Utilisation (per engine)
panels.description: Per-engine GPU busy % — MM's per-engine breakdown.

panels.title: GPU Throttle Reasons (per GT)
panels.description: xe DRM throttle flags (1 = actively throttling). 'any' = OR of all reasons; thermal is the headline for the T envelope. Via gpu_throttle_reader.py.

panels.title: DRAM Bandwidth (read/write/total) — NEW
panels.description: DRAM bandwidth via perf on IMC free-running counters (dram_bw_reader.py). Unit is GB/s.

panels.title: RAM Used / Available
panels.description: System memory used vs available (auto-scaled).

panels.title: RAM Stats
panels.description: Total / used bytes and utilisation.

panels.title: Disk Utilisation % (per device)
panels.description: rate(io_time)/10 → %busy. Loop/ram/dm/sr devices filtered.

panels.title: Disk Throughput (read/write)
panels.description: Per-device read/write throughput (auto-scaled to MB/s).

panels.title: Device Interrupt (IRQ) Rate (top devices)
panels.description: Per-device interrupt rate (numeric device IRQs only; housekeeping dropped).

panels.title: Network RX Throughput
panels.description: Per-interface receive throughput (auto-scaled).

panels.title: Network TX Throughput
panels.description: Per-interface transmit throughput (auto-scaled).

options.content: **R = Real-Time Determinism.** The C0-state residency panel below is always live (from `intel_powerstat`). Every other panel in this row comes from the opt-in **turbostat** plugin and populates only when `ENABLE_TURBOSTAT=true` (needs the kernel-matched `linux-tools` package) — otherwise they read *No data*, which is expected. Acronyms are spelled out in each panel title. **SMI** (System Management Interrupts) are the #1 hidden cause of RT latency spikes.

panels.title: CPU C0-state (active) Residency (per core)
panels.description: Time each core spent in the active C0 state — a determinism signal (deep C-states add wake-up latency). Source: intel_powerstat (always on).

panels.title: Instructions Per Cycle — IPC (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: IPC = Instructions Per Cycle. High = productive work each cycle; low = the core is 'busy' but stalled on memory. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: System Management Interrupts — SMI (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: SMI = System Management Interrupt: invisible firmware/BIOS CPU pauses, the #1 hidden cause of RT latency spikes. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Hardware Interrupts — IRQ (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: IRQ = Interrupt Request count per core over the sample interval. A core fielding heavy IRQs is a poor RT-thread home. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Non-Maskable Interrupts — NMI (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: NMI = Non-Maskable Interrupt count per core — cannot be deferred by the OS. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Per-core Temperature — CoreTmp (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Per-core die temperature. intel_powerstat is package-level; this exposes a single hot core (e.g. an RT executor pinned to it). Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Per-core Busy % (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Fraction of the interval the core ran in C0 (active). Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Per-core Frequency: Average vs Busy MHz (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Average MHz (over the whole interval) vs Busy MHz (only while running). A large gap means the core spent most of the interval idle/throttled. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Core Throttle events — CoreThr (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Thermal-throttle activations per core. Non-zero = the core hit a thermal limit and was clocked down. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: CPU Core C-state Residency: C1 / C6 / C7 (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Hardware C-state residency per core. Deeper states (C6/C7) save power but add wake-up latency — the core RT determinism trade-off. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: ACPI C-state Residency: C1 / C2 / C3 (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: ACPI = Advanced Configuration and Power Interface: the OS-visible C-state residency per core. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Power Breakdown — Package / Core / GPU / RAM / System Watts (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: turbostat's RAPL power domains: package, cores, graphics, RAM and the whole platform. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Package Deep-Idle Residency: PC2 / PC6 / PC10 (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Package (whole-SoC) deep-idle residency. PC10 is the deepest package sleep; high PC-state time means the entire SoC idled. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: System C0 (active) Residency: Total / Any-core / GPU (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Aggregate active-state residency: all cores summed, at-least-one-core active, and GPU active. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Low-Power Idle Residency — LPI: CPU / System (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: LPI = Low-Power Idle, the platform's deepest S0ix-style idle state. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Uncore & TSC Frequency (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Uncore (ring / last-level-cache / memory-controller) frequency, plus TSC = Time Stamp Counter reference frequency. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: Package Temperature — PkgTmp (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: Package-level temperature reported by turbostat. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.

panels.title: POLL Residency + CPU-GFX / RAM overlap (turbostat, opt-in)
panels.description: POLL = the shallow spin-idle state (no power saving, lowest wake latency). CPU+GFX = fraction where both CPU and graphics were active; RAM % = memory RAPL throttle. Needs ENABLE_TURBOSTAT.
